<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="Ubufox" /></noinclude><section begin=par104 />{{GHGheb|text=וּמֵ֖תִ}} is in closer logical connexion with what follows); {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=7|verse=4}} {{GHGheb|text=וָמַ֣הְנוּ שָׁ֔ם}}, {{GHGheb|text=וָמַ֑תָנוּ}} and {{GHGheb|text=וָמָֽתְנוּ}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ru|chapter=3|verse=3}} {{GHGheb|text=וָסַֹכְתְּ}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=10|verse=15}} {{GHGheb|text=וָ֝רָֹע}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=9|verse=4}} {{GHGheb|text=וָאַ֔יִן}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=13|verse=26}} {{GHGheb|text=וָלֹ֔א}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=47|verse=9}} {{GHGheb|text=וָחָ֔י}}; cf. also (with {{GHGterm|Ṭiphḥa}}) {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=33|verse=13}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=15|verse=12}}. The very frequent connexion of nouns expressing kindred ideas, by means of {{GHGheb|text=וָ}}, is due simply to considerations of rhythm, for even in such cases the {{GHGterm|Wāw}} must immediately precede the tone-syllable, which must be marked by a disjunctive accent, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=תֹּ֫הוּ וָבֹ֫הוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=1|verse=2}}, {{GHGheb|text=יוֹם וָלַ֫יְלָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=8|verse=22}} (see also the previous examples); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=13|verse=14}} (thrice); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=25|verse=3}} {{GHGheb|text=זָהָב נָכֶ֫סֶף}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=96|verse=7}} {{GHGheb|text=כָּבוֹד וָעֹז}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=76|verse=7}} {{GHGheb|text=וְרֶ֫כֶב וָסוּס}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=7|verse=13}} {{GHGheb|text=וְשֵׁם־וְחָם וָיֶ֫פֶת}}; {{GHGheb|text=נֹחַ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=21|verse=10}} {{GHGheb|text=כֹּה וָכֹה ;אֱלֹהִים וָמֶ֑לֶךְ|translate=thus and thus}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Est|chapter=1|verse=8}} {{GHGheb|text=אִישׁ־וָאִֽישׁ}} at the end of the verse, but in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=87|verse=5}} {{GHGheb|text=אִישׁ וְאִישׁ}} in spite of the {{GHGterm|D<sup>e</sup>ḥi}} with the second {{GHGheb|text=אִישׁ}}, because it is closely connected with the following predicate. Also with three words {{GHGheb|text=פַּ֫חַד וָפַ֫חַת וָפָ֑ה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=24|verse=17}}. On the other hand, the rapid pronunciation {{GHGheb|text=וְ}} occurs before a conjunctive accent (and, when farther removed from the principal pause, even with the smaller disjunctives, in spite of a following tone-syllable), e.g. {{GHGheb|text=צֹאן וְעֶ֣בֶד}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=32|verse=6}}; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=31|verse=40}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=7|verse=23}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=2|verse=21}}, and among the examples given above, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=7|verse=13}} and {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=76|verse=7}}. (Exceptions: {{GHGheb|text=וָקֵ֥דְמָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=13|verse=14}}, where evidently the {{GHGheb|text=וָ}} is intended to ensure the slow and solemn recitation of the promise, but also {{GHGheb|text=וָזִ֥יף}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=15|verse=55}}, {{GHGheb|text=וָעֵ֣תֶר}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=19|verse=7|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGheb|text=וָבֶ֥טֶן}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=19|verse=25|hidebook=1}}, all immediately before the pause.) For the same rhythmical reason {{GHGheb|text=וְ}} (not {{GHGheb|text=וָ}}) is used regularly with certain monosyllables which, by their nature, lean more closely upon the following word, thus {{GHGheb|text=וְזֶה}}, {{GHGheb|text=וְאֵת}}, {{GHGheb|text=וְגַם}}, {{GHGheb|text=וְלֹא}} (to be distinguished from {{GHGheb|text=וָלֹ֔א|translate=if not}}, with {{GHGterm|Zaqeph gadol}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=5|verse=17}}), and others.<section end=par104 />

<section begin=par105 />{{GHGpar-heading|105|Interjections}}

{{GHGmargin-letter|105|a}}
'''1.''' Among the interjections some (as in all languages) are simply natural sounds, or, as it were, vocal gestures, called forth involuntarily by certain impressions or sensations, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=אֲהָהּ}} ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=30|verse=2}} {{GHGheb|text=הָהּ}}), {{GHGheb|text=אָח|translate=ah!}} {{GHGheb|text=הֶאָח|translate=aha!}} (cf. this {{GHGheb|text=אָח}} also in {{GHGheb|text=אַחְלַי}} and {{GHGheb|text=אַֽחֲלֵי|translate=utinam!}}), {{GHGheb|text=אָֽנָּ֫א}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=32|verse=31}}, &c. ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=50|verse=17}} {{GHGheb|text=אָ֣נָּ֫א}}) ''ah!'' (from {{GHGheb|text=אָהּ}} and {{GHGheb|text=נָא}}), otherwise written {{GHGheb|text=אָֽנָּ֫ה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=20|verse=3}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jn|chapter=1|verse=14}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=116|verse=4}}; also {{GHGheb|text=הַס}} (in pause {{GHGheb|text=הָס}}, even in the plural {{GHGheb|text=הַ֫סּוּ|translate=hold your peace!}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Neh|chapter=8|verse=11}}) {{GHGtranslate|hush!}} {{GHGheb|text=הוֹי}} ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Am|chapter=5|verse=16}} {{GHGheb|text=הוֹ־הוֹ}}) {{GHGtranslate|ha! woe!}} {{GHGheb|text=אוֹי}}, {{GHGheb|text=א֫וֹיָה}} ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=120|verse=5}}), {{GHGheb|text=אִי}} (in {{GHGheb|text=אִילוֹ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ec|chapter=4|verse=10}}; {{GHGheb|text=אִי־לָךְ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ec|chapter=10|verse=16|hidebook=1}}) {{GHGtranslate|woe!}}

{{GHGmargin-letter|105|b}}
'''2.''' Others, however, originally expressed independent ideas, and become interjections only by rapid pronunciation and by usage, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=(הֵא) הֵן}} or {{GHGheb|text=הִנֵּה|translate=behold!}} (prop. {{GHGtranslate|here}}); {{GHGheb|text=רְאֵה|translate=behold!}} (prop. imperative); {{GHGheb|text=הָ֫בָה}}, plur. {{GHGheb|text=הָבוּ}} (prop. {{GHGtranslate|give}}, imperative of {{GHGheb|text=יָהַב}}; as to the tone, cf. {{GHGpar|69|o}}), {{GHGtranslate|come}}, the Latin {{GHGtranslate|age|en=do (2nd sg. imp.)}}, {{GHGtranslate|agite!|en=do (2nd pl. imp.)}} {{GHGheb|text=לְכָה}} (also {{GHGheb|text=לְךָ}}), {{GHGheb|text=לְכוּ}} (prop. {{GHGtranslate|go}}, imperative of {{GHGheb|text=הָלַךְ}}) with the same meaning<ref>{{GHGheb|text=רְאֵה}} ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=1|verse=8}}), {{GHGheb|text=הָ֫בָה}} and {{GHGheb|text=לְכָה}} are also used in connexion with the feminine and the plural, which proves that they have become quite stereotyped as interjections.</ref>; {{GHGheb|text=חָלִ֫ילָה|translate=far be it!}} (prop. ''ad profanum!'')<section end=par105 /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>
